$comment: Declares which Edge Function secrets each environment must have, and which
it must NOT have. Names only. A value must never appear in this file.
Checked by tools/check-secrets.mjs, which runs in the deploy workflows.
`forbidden` matters as much as `required`. Every mock flag compares against
the exact string "1", so a flag that is merely SET to something falsy still
works but is one typo away from silently disabling a paid integration or,
worse, silently enabling one. Production should not have them at all.
PLACES_MOCK being listed as forbidden in production is the launch
requirement expressed as a check rather than a line in a runbook.
SUPABASE_* keys are injected by the platform and are deliberately absent
from every list; see platformInjected below.

2026-09-12: staging and demo now call REAL Google for Places + Geocoding, so GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY moved from forbidden to required there and PLACES_MOCK / GEOCODE_MOCK are no longer required. Reason: both were mocked, which made Path discovery impossible to QA or demo (it returned nothing and looked broken). Each environment has its OWN Google key so usage is attributable. They still share one Google project quota; the calendar + transcribe mocks stay on.

staging.$comment: Places + Geocoding call REAL Google as of 2026-09-12, with staging's OWN key, because mocking them made Path discovery impossible to QA: it silently returned nothing and read as a broken product. AssemblyAI and both calendars stay mocked so staging still spends nothing there. Cost is bounded by the Google project's daily quota, which staging now shares with production. EMAIL_ALLOWLIST must be PRESENT and non-empty: the guard fails closed, so an absent allowlist means staging sends nothing at all, which looks like broken email rather than a safety feature.

demo.$comment: Same posture as staging, including a real Google key of its own (a demo that cannot show Path finding real businesses is not a demo). EMAIL_ALLOWLIST is set to an EMPTY string on purpose: the fail-closed guard then drops every recipient, so a sales demo can never email anyone.

production.$comment: EMAIL_ALLOWLIST is deliberately absent: APP_ENV=production short-circuits the guard, so an allowlist here would be read by nothing and would imply a restriction that does not apply. No mock flags at all. PLACES_MOCK is currently SET on production as a pre-launch cost saving, so this check FAILS today by design: it is the launch gate for plan Task 18, and it should stay failing until live Places has been verified behind a hard quota cap. OPS_NOTIFY_EMAIL is where notify_no_deals sends its operator heads-up digest; required on production only (the code degrades gracefully without it, so staging/demo do not need it), which means it must be set before this feature promotes to prod.
